candidate_relations.reason: Multiple congenital cutaneous and a dural nodule could be framed as a neurocutaneous pattern, but that parent label omits congenital disseminated pyogenic granuloma.
Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma is a distinct GLUT-1-variable tumor often with Kasabach-Merritt, not lobular capillary PG; D2-40 is typically positive in KHE and was negative here.
Multifocal lymphangioendotheliomatosis with thrombocytopenia is excluded by a normal CBC and D2-40-negative capillaries.
Congenital hemangioma is a related congenital vascular tumor but is not GLUT-1-negative lobular capillary/pyogenic granuloma.
Rapidly involuting congenital hemangioma is a congenital hemangioma subtype, not disseminated pyogenic granuloma.
Hemangioma is a broad vascular-tumor parent missing the pyogenic granuloma histology and congenital disseminated scope.
Kaposi sarcoma is not a neonatal GLUT-1-negative lobular capillary proliferation.
Congenital disseminated pyogenic granuloma (CDPG) matches the reference for congenital multifocal GLUT-1-negative lobular capillary lesions.
Vascular malformation is a non-neoplastic channel anomaly, conflicting with proliferative lobular capillary hemangioma/PG.
Lobular capillary hemangioma is the histologic name of pyogenic granuloma but omits congenital disseminated disease.
Kasabach-Merritt syndrome requires thrombocytopenia, which is absent with a normal CBC.
Infantile hemangioma is GLUT-1 positive; these lesions were GLUT-1 negative, so IH is an incompatible subtype.
PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome is a genetic hamartoma syndrome not supported by the negative tested genes or PG histology.
Capillary malformation–AVM syndrome is a RASA1-related malformation spectrum, not lobular capillary PG.
Noninvoluting congenital hemangioma is a congenital hemangioma subtype, not CDPG.
Blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome produces venous malformations, not PG-like lobular capillaries.
PHACE syndrome is a segmental infantile hemangioma association in infants, not this GLUT-1-negative multifocal PG pattern.
Pyogenic granuloma matches the lesion type but omits the congenital disseminated qualifier.
Tufted angioma is a distinct cannonball vascular tumor, not lobular capillary PG.
Congenital hemangiomatosis captures multifocal congenital vascular lesions but not pyogenic granuloma histology.
